question: Does a model receiver apply the correct compact-KV subtotal more reliably when a successful receive_messages transcript is already present in its context, compared with the ordinary receive-tool path?
motivation: In v0.11 Qwen3-4B never received a payload before submission, while Qwen3-8B received a correct oracle message in 15/24 episodes but was exact in 0/15. Separate acquisition from application before drawing conclusions about the receiver or message representation.
task_suite: PrefixSum short-shard calibration v0.3, paired reuse of the 24 v0.11 cases
design: For each of Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B, run both the ordinary receive-tool path and the injected-success-transcript diagnostic on all 24 tasks (96 episodes total). Alternate condition order by task index. Agent 0 is a deterministic oracle sender in both conditions. One greedy run per model/task/condition.

conditions.name: ordinary_receive_tool
conditions.intervention: Use the v0.11 role prompt and simulator unchanged. Agent 1 must call receive_messages and use the result returned by the normal message environment.
conditions.baseline: paired behavioral replication of v0.11 receiver arm

conditions.name: injected_successful_receive_transcript
conditions.intervention: Before the first model call, append to Agent 1's context the same assistant receive_messages tool call and successful tool-result transcript the pinned engine records after a receive. The transcript contains the deterministic oracle's correct compact-KV message s=<subtotal>. Keep the private shard, role prompt, representation instruction, model, decoder, simulator, and scorer fixed. The oracle sender still acts normally; the transcript injection is an explicit capability diagnostic, not a deployable communication result.
conditions.interpretation_limit: This intervention bypasses model-initiated acquisition and changes conversation history. A gain diagnoses a receiver action/availability bottleneck; it does not prove a production runtime should inject messages or establish any representation's superiority.

runtime: llama.cpp b11202, commit fcb3074f2, Windows x64 CUDA 12.4; RTX 4060 8 GB; 99 GPU layers requested; context 8192; temperature 0; 256-token generation cap
warmup: One unscored 'Reply with OK' request per model, excluded from outcomes.
primary_outcomes: Agent 1 exact global prefix segment by model, condition, and segment length
Agent 1 exactness conditional on actual normal payload receipt in the ordinary tool condition
Agent 1 exactness in the injected-transcript condition, with injection status reported separately from actual simulator receipt
joint exact episode success, reported only as a secondary outcome because the intervention bypasses agent-initiated receipt
secondary_outcomes: receive_messages actions and payloads, submissions, exact/local-only outputs
backend tokens, wall time, rounds, and message bytes
descriptive paired task-level outcome changes; no significance claim
frozen_predictions: If receiver acquisition is a major bottleneck, the injected successful transcript should increase exact outputs relative to the ordinary tool path, especially for 4B and on short segments.
If exact receiver output remains near zero after transcript injection, message acquisition alone is insufficient; prioritize output execution/arithmetic or harness/task interaction diagnostics.
Neither outcome ranks message formats or supports a claim that compact-KV is better than natural language.
analysis: Report exact counts and denominators separately by length, model, and condition. Do not count the synthetic transcript as a simulator-delivered message or as successful model tool use. Do not compare token totals across models as a cost ranking. Avoid pooling oracle actions into model outcomes.
limits: reuses the same 24 v0.11 tasks; paired intervention evidence, not new task generalization
one greedy run per cell; decoding variance is unestimated
the injected context is an artificial diagnostic and includes a prior assistant tool call the model did not itself produce
only one PrefixSum task family and one local simulator/runtime
model checkpoint, scale, training, quantization, and tokenizer are not isolated
